newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania's Hermis Bank sees better 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania's Hermis Bank sees better 1996 profit.

text.p: Lithuania's second largest commercial bank, Hermis Bank, said on Wednesday that its 1996 profit would be better than expected.
Nadiezda Novickiene, in an interview with Reuters, also said the bank's board would ask shareholders to cover the 1995 loss with the profits from 1996.

"Our results for 1996 are much better than what we planned, which was a net profit of 12 million litas," she said, adding that the bank would not reveal the exact figure until after the March 28 general shareholders' meeting.
The market expects Hermis' 1996 profit to be around 25 million litas after a loss of over eight million in 1995.
"We on the board hope that the shareholders will agree to cover the 1995 loss with the profit from 1996 instead of paying out dividends," Novickiene said.

Hermis last year paid out dividends on the basis of the results of its Lithuanian audit, which showed a profit of 3.6 million litas. But an international audit conducted by Arthur Andersen showed a loss of over eight million litas.
Hermis Bank's share capital at the end of last year was 67 million litas and its assets were worth 541.9 million litas.
The bank's shareholders decided last month to boost its share capital to 90 million litas.
The bank would consider buying into the country's state banks, which are slated for privatisation, Novickiene said.

"If the price was right, we would consider buying a stake in the state banks," she said. "We are more interested in banks that are working well, but the state banks have a good branch network, which is attractive."
The Lithuanian government said that it will privatise two of the country's three huge state-run banks, the State Commercial Bank and the Agriculture Bank.
The government had to inject 165 million litas of fresh capital into the State Commercial Bank last year to save it from a liquidity crisis sparked by bad loans.
Novickiene also said Hermis would boost its share capital one more time this year.
The bank's shareholders last month agreed to raise its share capital from 67 million litas to 90 million litas.
"The new share capital will be registered at the central bank in two weeks' time," Novickiene said.
She added that the new shares were being sold at a price higher than their nominal value.
Hermis Bank's shares on the Vilnius bourse are currently trading at 195 litas, almost four times their nominal value of 50 litas.
Novickiene added that Hermis bank had plans to open a representative office in Moscow soon.
